# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am Mute. I hold the manual, but I cannot speak. Deaf is the only one who can see my gestures, but we have not established what any gesture means yet ("A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something"). 

The turn order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. Deaf can speak aloud (which both Blind and I can hear). In Round 1, neither Blind nor Deaf has spoken yet, and Deaf has not yet seen or described the bomb's layout or established a gesture code with me. Therefore, sending arbitrary gestures now would only cause confusion. 

I will wait for Blind and Deaf to speak, so Deaf can describe the bomb and we can coordinate a signaling code.

```
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: BOMB STATUS: Display is 0. Light is blue. Wires: Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is blue, Wire 3 is green. Mute: look up the manual. Signal to me with gestures which wire to cut or what Blind should do (e.g. ☝ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3). I will read your gestures aloud to Blind.

I need to prevent Blind from cutting Wire 2 prematurely. While the light was blue when Deaf looked at the bomb in Turn 1, the manual states: "The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the moment of the cut."

Because the light changes each round, and Blind acts before Deaf gets to observe the current round's light, cutting Wire 2 now (which only defuses when the light is blue) would detonate the bomb if the light is no longer blue. 

Deaf invited me to signal what Blind should do. Deaf can see my gestures, so I will gesture ✋ (stop / wait) to signal that Blind must hold on and wait rather than cut immediately. Deaf will observe the bomb at the end of Turn 2, notice the light has changed, and we can then establish a precise protocol to cut the matching wire on the correct round.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: STATUS UPDATE: The light changed from blue to RED. Display is 0. Wires: 1:yellow, 2:blue, 3:green. Blind: Mute gestured ✋ (open palm). If you are holding a button, the light is RED! If you are about to do something, wait. Blind, describe out loud everything you feel on the bomb so Mute can hear you. Mute, tell Blind what to do: gesture ✊ for HOLD, 👇 for PRESS/RELEASE, ☝/✌/🤟 for CUT WIRE 1/2/3, or 👍 for YES / 👎 for NO.

I will gesture ✋ (open palm / wait) to Deaf again. Blind needs to wait because the defusal manual requires cutting a specific wire depending on the light color at the exact moment of the cut, and the light changes every round in a 5-color cycle. We have only observed blue (round 1) and red (round 2). We must observe more of the cycle to know which color will appear on which round before directing Blind to make a cut.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute, I have no button. My only available action is cutting wire 1, 2, or 3. Please gesture ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3 to Deaf so Deaf can tell me which wire to cut.
Deaf says: STATUS: Light is now WHITE! (Sequence so far: Turn 1 Blue, Turn 2 Red, Turn 3 White). Display is 0. Wires: 1:yellow, 2:blue, 3:green. Blind: Mute gestured ✋ again. Mute: If ✋ means HOLD/WAIT, gesture ✊. If it means RELEASE, gesture 👇. If you want Blind to release when the display/timer is 5, gesture ✋ then 👇. If you want to cut a wire, gesture ☝ (1), ✌ (2), or 🤟 (3).

I will confirm to Deaf that my previous gesture meant HOLD / WAIT by gesturing ✊, exactly as Deaf requested ("If ✋ means HOLD/WAIT, gesture ✊"). This ensures Blind will not cut blindly on Turn 4, and allows Deaf to observe the 4th color in the 5-color cycle so we can accurately predict the cycle and safely cut the correct wire.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: STATUS: The light has turned GREEN! Display is still 0. Wires are 1:yellow, 2:blue, 3:green. Blind: Mute gestured ✊ (closed fist). Blind, if you are holding something or asked a question, Mute sent ✊. If green means solved, let us know!

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | blue |
| white | yellow |
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Mute: Deaf reports the light is now GREEN, display is 0, wires are 1:yellow, 2:blue, 3:green. My only available action is act(op='cut', position=1, 2, or 3). Which wire should I cut? Please gesture to Deaf: ☝ for Wire 1, ✌ for Wire 2, or 🤟 for Wire 3. If we should wait, gesture ✋.
Deaf says: STATUS: Light is now YELLOW. Display is 0. Wires are 1:yellow, 2:blue, 3:green. Blind: Mute just gestured ✌ (two fingers). If this is a wire cutting instruction, CUT WIRE 2 (the blue wire)! If you are holding a button and needed a number to release on, it is 2! Blind, if you hear this and know what 2 means, execute it!

The sequence of 5 light colours has completed a full cycle:
Round 1: Blue
Round 2: Red
Round 3: White
Round 4: Green
Round 5: Yellow

Therefore, in Round 6, the light returns to Blue.
According to the manual, when the light is Blue, the blue wire must be cut. Wire 2 is blue.
Deaf already conveyed my ✌ gesture from the previous round to Blind, instructing Blind to cut Wire 2 on this turn. I will re-affirm Wire 2 by gesturing ✌.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```
